description:
Measured from the public causal stream (HEAD efa05d386, debug interp):

    00420:      5,356 transport_shape + 5,070 callable_construction of 12,645
                total settlements (82%); ~22 + ~21 per backend executable (239)
    predsearch: 2,397 + 2,325 of 6,770 (70%... 82% incl. slots)
    rangemap:     749 +   716 of 2,061 (71%)

Each settles ONCE with changed=true (no churn -- keys are distinct), cache-hit
rates are tiny (3%), displacement zero. So this is honest one-time work; the
question is whether the POPULATION is proportional: ~45 products per executable
for a ~40-function program. If two positions with the same structural need each
run their own product only to intern the same ShapeId, the product key is
per-position where per-structure would do -- fold candidates per
feedback_fold_concordant_ideas.

## Task
Audit what the per-key work actually derives: histogram the product keys by
their resulting ShapeId/CallableId; count how many distinct results the 10k
products produce on 00420. If results collapse heavily, re-key the products by
structural need and measure the settlement-count drop. If they do not collapse,
close this with the numbers as the proportionality justification.

## Checks
- Either settlements drop materially with identical canonical programs, or the
  ticket closes documenting measured 1:1 key-to-result proportionality.
title: Transport-shape and callable-construction products are 82% of all settlements: proportionality audit
